text: Plans A and B from the LABT review, tested on journal 1-min bars Oct 7-28 (1,270 stock-days, summer session 13:30-20:00 UTC). Plan A: after price breaks the pre-market high (PMH) by 2%, first bar within 120 min whose low comes within 3% of PMH and closes back above it; buy next bar open; stop 1% under that bar's low. Plan B: break of the first-5-min high by 0.5% on a bar with volume >= the prior 10-bar average; buy at ORH+1%; stop 1% under the breakout bar low (min 3%). Both: sell half at +20%, rest on the first 5-min close under the 5-min 9 EMA, else stop or the close; a bar hitting stop and target counts as stop. LABT-like days (pre-market high 30%+ above the first pre-market print): A n=9, 1 winner (MNDR Oct 12 +22%), avg -1.1%; B n=38, 29% winners, avg +0.2% (winners avg +13%, losers -5%). All stock-days: A n=181, 24% winners, avg +1.1%; B n=208, 29% winners, avg +0.7%. About 70% of trades in both were stopped out. With ~2% round-trip commission on ~$50 positions, every group is negative (A pm30 -3.1%, B pm30 -1.8%, A all -0.9%, B all -1.2%; corrected Nov 7, the first summary mislabelled 'other' as 'all'). Same-bar stop and target: only 1 of 389 trades had a 1-min bar touching both; re-run with candle direction (green bar = low first, red bar = high first) changed B all from +0.74% to +0.80% gross, nothing else. LABT Nov 5 (A about +30%) was the exception in this data.
